feedback.problem:
Fill in the missing parts in the parametric equations below that describe all the points on the line segment $\overset{―}{PQ},$ where $P(-4,-2,4)$ and $Q(0,8,3).$

| $x=$ | {{field-1}} | $t\in [$ {{field-2}} $,1]$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $y=$ | $-2+10t$ |  |
| $z=$ | {{field-3}} |  |
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we need to find a direction vector that is parallel to the line passing through the given points. We can use the vector $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{PQ} \\  & =\overset{\to }{OQ}-\overset{\to }{OP} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 8 \\ 3\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -2 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 10 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the vector equation of the line is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 10 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}4t \\ 10t \\ -t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-4+4t \\ -2+10t \\ 4-t\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

To get the equations for the line segment, we take only $t\in [0,1].$ Notice that substitution of $t=0$ in the above equation gives the coordinates of $P$ and substitution of $t=1$ gives the coordinates of $Q.$

Therefore, the parametric equations of the line segment $\overset{―}{PQ}$ are the following:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=-4+4t \\ y=-2+10t \\ z=4-t\end{aligned}\,\,t\in [0,1]
$$
